$sources: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 1.2.5, Table 6.1.2 and notes a-h (pp. 482-483)
source: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 1.2.5 (p. 482): member deflections within Table 6.1.2, storey drift and sway by Sec 1.5.6, under the service combinations of Sec 2.7.5

storeyDrift.source: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 1.5.6.1(a) (pp. 499-500): storey drift for loads other than earthquake ≤ 0.005h for T < 0.7 s, 0.004h for T ≥ 0.7 s, 0.0025h for unreinforced masonry; T as used for the base shear (Sec 2.5.7.2); under the wind service combination D + 0.5L + 0.7W (Sec 2.7.5, p. 686)

sway.source: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 1.5.6.2 (p. 500): overall sway at the top level due to wind ≤ H/500, H the height above ground, under D + 0.5L + 0.7W (Sec 2.7.5 combination 3, p. 686)

roofPlasterCeiling.label: Roof member supporting a plaster ceiling

roofOtherCeiling.label: Roof member supporting a non-plaster ceiling

roofNoCeiling.label: Roof member not supporting a ceiling

wallBrittle.label: Exterior wall or interior partition member, brittle finishes

wallFlexible.label: Exterior wall or interior partition member, flexible finishes

metalSheeting.label: Structural roofing or siding of formed metal sheets
metalSheeting.source: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Table 6.1.2 note a (p. 482): total load deflection ≤ l/60

metalRoofSecondary.label: Secondary roof member (purlin) supporting formed metal roofing
metalRoofSecondary.source: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Table 6.1.2 note a (p. 482): live load deflection ≤ l/150; only where the metal sheets have no roof covering

metalWallSecondary.label: Secondary wall member (girt) supporting formed metal siding
metalWallSecondary.source: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Table 6.1.2 note a (p. 482): design wind load deflection ≤ l/90

deflection.source: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 1.2.5, Table 6.1.2 (pp. 482-483), columns L, W (note f) and D + L (notes d, g); note c: a cantilever's l is twice its length; Sec 10.12.3 (part 2 p. 172) refers steel members to these limits

overturning.note: the base overturning moment (Eq 6.1.1, Eq 6.2.47) at most 2/3 of the dead load resisting moment, so a factor of safety of 1.5; the weight of earth over the footings that the code allows is left out and E is taken at its design level (1.0E), both on the safe side; foundations themselves may be designed for 3/4 of the seismic overturning moment (Sec 2.5.7.8)
overturning.source: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 1.2.10 (p. 485), Sec 1.5.5 Eq 6.1.1 (p. 499), Sec 1.8.4 (p. 507): base overturning moment ≤ 2/3 of the dead load resisting moment; Sec 2.5.7.8 Eq 6.2.47 (p. 632)
